title: Azure Load Balancer Health Probe Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:metrics` events with `metricName="ProbeHealthStatus" namespace="Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.14 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:metrics` traffic without `metricName="ProbeHealthStatus" namespace="Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers"`. Confirm UC-4.2.14 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:metrics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" metricName="ProbeHealthStatus" namespace="Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.14_azure_load_balancer_heal_14"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.14 — Azure Load Balancer Health Probe Failures: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:metrics` for search criteria `metricName="ProbeHealthStatus" namespace="Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Load Balancer Health Probe Failures' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.14 drives critical-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: ProbeHealthStatus 1 = healthy, 0 = unhealthy. Alert when any backend pool shows unhealthy. Correlate with VM availability and application logs. Monitor SNAT exhaustion (SnatConnectionCount) for outbound issues.
visualization: Status panel (probe health), Table (LB, backend, status), Timeline.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:metrics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
ProbeHealthStatus 1 = healthy, 0 = unhealthy. Alert when any backend pool shows unhealthy. Correlate with VM availability and application logs. Monitor SNAT exhaustion (SnatConnectionCount) for outbound issues.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" metricName="ProbeHealthStatus" namespace="Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.14_azure_load_balancer_heal_14"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:metrics` in `index=azure` to detect azure load balancer health probe failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_14_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Status panel (probe health), Table (LB, backend, status), Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure load balancer health probe failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
